prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has knee injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1048; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Good afternoon. This is the adjuster calling about the rear-end collision you reported in Sugar Land. Is this a good time to record a statement?

A: Yes, that's fine. Go ahead.

Q: Thank you. Please state your full name and confirm you're the driver of the vehicle that was struck from behind.

A: I'm the driver. I was in my own car, stopped at a light on the main road heading toward the shopping center.

Q: Understood. Tell me what happened right before the impact.

A: I was stopped behind a white sedan. The light was red. I felt a jolt and my head snapped forward and back. I looked in the mirror and saw a pickup right on my bumper.

Q: Did you notice the pickup approaching before the collision?

A: Not really. I was watching the light and my phone was in the cup holder. I didn't see it until it was too late.

Q: How fast do you think it was moving when it hit you?

A: It didn't seem like a huge speed, but it was enough to push me into the sedan ahead.

Q: Where did you feel pain first?

A: My right knee. It hit the dashboard. Over the next day it swelled up and I couldn't bend it all the way.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment for the knee?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the same evening and I've had follow-up visits with my family doctor. I'm doing physical therapy twice a week now.

Q: Did you have any knee problems before this collision?

A: No, nothing that stopped me from working or exercising.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you'd like to add about the accident?

A: Just that I'm still having trouble with stairs and driving for long stretches. I'd like the claim handled as quickly as possible.

Q: Understood. I'll follow up with the documents we discussed. Thank you for your time.

A: Thanks. Have a good day.
